extracted_findings: RPC graph and performance measurements support counterfactual diagnosis and resource actuation. Experiments inject resource interference and software faults in microservice applications.
limitations: The incomplete-instrumentation experiment retains per-tier latency and end-to-end measurements. Concurrent independent causes are harder than single causes.
reviewer_implication: Do not equate missing internal instrumentation with missing observations of an entire layer.
quality_rationale: Baselines require different instrumentation. Tested faults and platforms bound transfer. Repeated independent deployment variation is not established by the assessed sections.

extracted_findings: Matches spans through timing distributions, call-graph constraints and joint optimisation. Evaluates benchmark applications and transformed Alibaba trace data, including load and dynamic call behaviour.
limitations: Request/response observations and test traces are required. Alibaba data are separated by call graph and inter-arrival times compressed. Reconstruction is not direct evidence of a cause.
reviewer_implication: Record whether a request link is explicit or inferred, and test ambiguity when identifiers are absent.
quality_rationale: Comparator assumptions differ. Production evaluation transforms sampled data. Useful ablations and load variation are reported, but this does not validate arbitrary cross-platform log correlation.

extracted_findings: Structural graph plus regression-based hypothesis testing ranks root-cause metrics. Oracle evaluation: 99 incidents, AC@1 0.404 and AC@5 0.763. Simulations assess graph and fault-strength variation.
limitations: Metric ranking differs from component diagnosis. Architecture knowledge and metric mapping are needed. Some baseline information and sampling assumptions differ.
reviewer_implication: Separate root-cause metric, component and fault explanation in the evaluation.
quality_rationale: Original baseline implementations do not all receive their original operator information or sampling rate. Real evaluation is one database context, with additional simulated robustness checks.

extracted_findings: Compares causal discovery and RCA on synthetic data and microservice testbeds. Studies graph accuracy, diagnostic performance, runtime and input length, with repeated experiments.
limitations: CIRCA uses a PC-derived graph because its structural graph is unavailable. Limited fault types and benchmark systems constrain generalisation.
reviewer_implication: Compare simple baselines and test uncertain failure times. Do not assume causal modelling is inherently more accurate.
quality_rationale: Extensive comparison and repetition, but adapted inputs and implementation choices prevent treating every result as a direct replication of the original method.

source_locations: Sections 4-7, Tables 2 and 5, PDF pp. 3-5 and 8-9
extracted_findings: Ranks anomalous SIEM windows using severity, direction and action context, and 62 count/rate/distribution features. Evaluates about 29.4 million firewall/IDS events with rolling weekly tests.
limitations: Ground truth is not exhaustive. Ten-minute windows and eight-week training periods may not suit a low-traffic PoC. Context features alone do not consistently improve detection.
reviewer_implication: Treat aggregation window and feature usefulness as hypotheses to test against available events.
quality_rationale: Temporal evaluation and component comparisons are described. Partially labelled private enterprise data limit completeness and independent replication.

source_locations: Sections III-IV, Tables I-II, PDF pp. 3-5
extracted_findings: Reconstructs dataset-generation steps and evaluates original and corrected flow data. Finds flow-construction and labelling defects and shortcut learning. Per-class outcomes change despite near-identical aggregate accuracy.
limitations: Findings concern one dataset and particular reconstruction and classifier choices, not every intrusion dataset.
reviewer_implication: Check fault injection and labels independently. Report scenario-level outcomes and examine misleading features.
quality_rationale: Reconstruction and comparative experiments are inspectable. Dataset and model scope bound transfer beyond the studied benchmark.

source_locations: Sections 3-4 and Table 2, PDF pp. 4-7 (arXiv v1)
extracted_findings: Uses counters and sampled traffic for triage, then packet-derived evidence summaries and constrained reports. Representative replay windows include wrong attributions with high self-reported confidence.
limitations: One illustrative replay table is not an overall accuracy estimate. No comparative evidence establishes production effectiveness or safe automated repair.
reviewer_implication: Validate evidence references separately from the diagnosis and do not treat model confidence as calibrated probability.
quality_rationale: Method is described, but the small illustrative evaluation lacks comprehensive comparison and repeated-run coverage. Claims about scalability are not established by this experiment.

extracted_findings: Handlers collect diagnostics and retrieve historical incidents for root-cause categorisation. Uses 653 incidents with a 75/25 split. GPT-4 micro-F1 is 0.766, macro-F1 0.533. More context is not always better.
limitations: Private single-service labelled data and imbalanced categories limit transfer. Collection-module deployment scale must not be confused with equivalent deployment of LLM prediction.
reviewer_implication: Compare evidence selection and report per-scenario results. Separate collection time from model inference time.
quality_rationale: Ablations and three rounds are reported. One service, private labels, model choice and historical similarity remain limitations.

extracted_findings: Controller and expert agents use bounded tools and observation snapshots. Evaluation uses 161 selected anomalous Flink jobs. Semantic and LLM-based scores, action validity and trajectory completion are distinct outcomes.
limitations: Tool and observation changes accompany the multi-agent design, so agent count is not isolated. LLM scoring and class-balanced selection affect interpretation. Proposed fixes are not executed repairs.
reviewer_implication: Compare architectures with matched data and budgets, and measure evidence correctness and invalid actions separately.
quality_rationale: Engineer-reviewed annotations and leakage controls are described. Several architectural changes and surrogate output scores limit causal attribution to agent organisation.

extracted_findings: Aligns metric time series with textual representations and retrieves incident examples. Reports multiple-choice diagnosis accuracy separately from GPT-4o-judged report win rates. Some short-sequence results favour baselines.
limitations: Fixed-seed offline evaluation, augmented series and an LLM report judge limit operational conclusions. Report preference is not diagnosis accuracy.
reviewer_implication: Keep explanation ratings separate from verified diagnostic correctness.
quality_rationale: Dataset and metric definitions are supplied. Augmentation, fixed seed and lack of live evaluation constrain robustness and transfer claims.

extracted_findings: Provides live fault-injection tasks for detection, localisation, RCA and mitigation. Compares agent behaviour, correctness, time, steps and tokens. More steps do not consistently improve performance.
limitations: The evaluated Flash implementation is simplified. Task definitions and selected problem sets affect comparisons. The reported selected-problem count and task-table denominators require care and are not pooled here.
reviewer_implication: Separate task outcomes, include a no-fault control and track cost and failed tool calls.
quality_rationale: Live evaluation and task definitions are useful. Reconstructed baselines, problem selection and reporting granularity qualify comparative conclusions.

extracted_findings: Separates diagnostic and writer roles and uses reversible action stacks. GPT-4o solves 9/13 AIOpsLab mitigation tasks, versus 2/13 without retry and 3/13 with retry without undo.
limitations: Eight ITBench successes exploit non-persistent injected faults. Faithful undo and severity measurement are assumptions. Human approval support is described, but its effectiveness is not established by a user study.
reviewer_implication: Test persistent faults, actual recovery, approval boundaries and rollback outcomes independently.
quality_rationale: Ablation supports undo-and-retry in the tested tasks. Small task sets, benchmark artefacts and differences in baseline provenance constrain generalisation.

extracted_findings: Evaluates 90 live scenarios with three runs per agent-model configuration. Distinguishes diagnosis, mitigation and joint success. Added noise reduces diagnosis success for each configuration.
limitations: Different agents also have different models and tools. LLM-judge agreement is checked on a sample, not proof of an error-free oracle. One benchmark family cannot establish general production reliability.
reviewer_implication: Use repeated runs, distracting symptoms, a clear diagnosis rubric and independent recovery checks.
quality_rationale: Repeated runs and a human-labelled oracle-validation sample support appraisal. Architecture, tool and model differences confound a universal agent ranking.
